blocks.x: The platform as a product with developers as customers: golden paths published as versioned APIs, scaffolds that carry SLOs and budgets by default, bypass reasons logged and answered — adoption earned through experience, never mandated.
Adoption is the metric; everything else is the product roadmap

Platform engineering exists to make the right thing the easy thing: a new service should inherit observability, security defaults, SLOs and cost budgets because it rode a golden path — not because a hero wired them by hand. The platform team runs this as a product with a roadmap, SLAs and customers: your engineers.

The funnel is the honest measure: time from repo creation to first production deploy, adoption of paths versus off-path workarounds, and the platform NPS that tells you whether engineers would fight to keep it.

Below: the failure modes that make internal platforms mandatory-but-bypassed, the reference architecture of paths-as-products, and the console that tracks adoption honestly — including why people leave the path.
Four ways internal platforms become mandatory-but-bypassed
Each failure mode drives a quiet fork around the platform — the countermeasures log the bypass reasons and fix the platform until leaving is harder than staying.

widgets.title: The internal developer platform — click nodes for the offered contract

nodes.label: Service portal
nodes.detail: Every service's page: ownership, scorecard, SLOs, dependencies, runbook links — the catalog is the front door and it must never lie.

nodes.label: Golden template
nodes.detail: Versioned service scaffold with the inheritance pack built in; template releases carry changelogs and migration notes.

nodes.label: Environment provisioning
nodes.detail: Declarative environment requests through policy gates — a new environment is a pull request, not a ticket.

nodes.label: Deployment rails
nodes.detail: Progressive delivery configured by default: canary, analysis, automatic rollback on budget breach.

nodes.label: Observability defaults
nodes.detail: Dashboards, alerts and trace wiring born with the service — a service without telemetry cannot leave the template.

nodes.label: Scorecards
nodes.detail: Maturity computed from evidence (security, reliability, docs, deps, cost, ops) — visible to everyone, reviewed quarterly.

nodes.label: Exception registry
nodes.detail: Off-path deployments documented, owned and expiry-dated — the exception review is where standards evolve.

widgets.note: Click nodes for the contract each rail offers. The exception registry feeds the template roadmap — standards evolve from real exceptions, not from committees.
